text: The headaches started two weeks ago and have been getting worse, especially in the mornings. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; since the stress test and wall motion abnormalities are confirmed, we must determine if your symptoms stem from cardiac insufficiency or a neurological issue. Given the morning worsening of headaches and visual flashes, have you noticed any severe neck stiffness, nausea, or a sudden "thunderclap" onset of pain?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I do not have any neck stiffness, nausea, or sudden thunderclap headaches. The pain has been a gradual throbbing that is worst when I wake up in the morning.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast to evaluate for posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) or mass effect. REQUEST TEST: CT Head with contrast to rule out acute hemorrhage or venous sinus thrombosis.

You mentioned confirmed wall motion abnormalities on stress testing; does your headache severity correlate with any changes in your blood pressure readings at home, and have you noticed any swelling in your hands or feet?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast: Evidence of increased intracranial pressure with signs compatible with idiopathic intracranial hypertension. No masses or lesions observed. CT Head with contrast: No acute hemorrhage or venous sinus thrombosis observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) with confirmed cardiac wall motion abnormalities likely due to a separate, chronic cardiac issue unrelated to the current neurological presentation. The headache and visual flashes are driven by the increased intracranial pressure seen on the MRI, not the heart condition.
